title: Maximum Number of Words Found in Sentences
statement: Each string in `sentences` is one sentence: lowercase words joined by exactly one space each, with no space at the start or the end. Count the words of every sentence and return the largest of these counts.
constraints: sentences[i] contains only lowercase English letters and spaces
sentences[i] has no leading or trailing space
Words in sentences[i] are separated by exactly one space

examples.name: Example 1
input: this is great thanks very much

tests.name: Test 3
input: a b c d e f g h i j

tests.name: Test 6
input: a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x

notes:
## Intuition

Because words are always joined by exactly one space and no sentence starts or ends with a space, a sentence with `k` spaces has exactly `k + 1` words. So there is no need to split strings into word lists: counting spaces is enough. The answer is the largest such count over all sentences.

## Approach

1. Start `most` at 0.
2. For each `sentence`, start `words` at 1 (every sentence has at least one word).
3. Walk the characters; every space `ch === ' '` marks the start of one more word, so add 1 to `words`.
4. After the sentence, keep the larger of `most` and `words`.
5. Return `most`.

## Example 1, step by step

- `"alice and bob love leetcode"` has 4 spaces, so `words = 5` and `most = 5`.
- `"i think so too"` has 3 spaces, so `words = 4`; `most` stays 5.
- `"this is great thanks very much"` has 5 spaces, so `words = 6` and `most = 6`.

The answer is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L), where L is the total number of characters, since each character is looked at once.
- Space: O(1): only two counters are kept.

## Pitfalls

- Start `words` at 1, not 0: the last word of a sentence is not followed by a space.
- Splitting on spaces also works here, but builds an array for every sentence; counting avoids that extra memory.
- Several sentences can tie for the maximum; only the count is returned, so ties need no handling.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `most` | the largest word count seen so far |
| `sentence` | the sentence being examined |
| `words` | word count of the current sentence (spaces + 1) |
| `ch` | the current character |

narration.2: No sentence has been counted yet, so the best count starts at 0.
narration.3: Look at the sentences one at a time.
narration.4: A sentence always has at least one word, so its count starts at 1.
narration.5: Scan every character of the sentence.
narration.6: A space always sits between two words...
narration.7: ...so each space adds one more word.
narration.10: Keep the larger of the best so far and this sentence's count.
narration.12: Every sentence has been counted; return the largest count.
